claim: The mitotic exit network (MEN) is a GTPase signaling cascade in budding yeast.
source: In budding yeast, the mitotic exit network (MEN), a GTPase signaling cascade, integrates spatial and temporal cues to promote exit from mitosis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of the MEN.

claim: The MEN integrates spatial and temporal cues to promote exit from mitosis.
source: In budding yeast, the mitotic exit network (MEN), a GTPase signaling cascade, integrates spatial and temporal cues to promote exit from mitosis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a function of the MEN.

claim: The MEN effector protein Cdc14 resides in the nucleolus.
source: This signal integration requires transmission of a signal generated on the cytoplasmic face of spindle pole bodies (SPBs; yeast equivalent of centrosomes) to the nucleolus, where the MEN effector protein Cdc14 resides.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the subcellular localization of Cdc14.

claim: The MEN activating signal at SPBs is relayed to Cdc14 in the nucleolus through the dynamic localization of Dbf2-Mob1.
source: Here, we show that the MEN activating signal at SPBs is relayed to Cdc14 in the nucleolus through the dynamic localization of its terminal kinase complex Dbf2-Mob1.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Cdc15 regulates nuclear access of Dbf2-Mob1.
source: Cdc15, the protein kinase that activates Dbf2-Mob1 at SPBs, also regulates its nuclear access.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Cdc5 priming phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1 targets Dbf2-Mob1 to the nucleolus.
source: Once in the nucleus, priming phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1, the nucleolar anchor of Cdc14, by the Polo-like kinase Cdc5 targets Dbf2-Mob1 to the nucleolus.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Nucleolar Dbf2-Mob1 phosphorylates Cfi1/Net1 and Cdc14, activating Cdc14.
source: Nucleolar Dbf2-Mob1 then phosphorylates Cfi1/Net1 and Cdc14, activating Cdc14.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The MEN is the budding yeast homolog of the Hippo pathway.
source: The mitotic exit network (MEN), a Ras-like GTPase kinase signaling cascade and budding yeast homolog of the Hippo pathway (Hergovich and Hemmings, 2012), represents such an example for signaling across cellular compartments.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Budding yeast undergoes a closed mitosis without disassembling the nuclear envelope and nucleolus.
source: Because budding yeast undergoes a closed mitosis without disassembling the nuclear envelope and nucleolus, the MEN must transmit a signal generated at the cytoplasmic face of SPBs, across the nuclear envelope and into the nucleolus to activate its effector Cdc14.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a characteristic of budding yeast mitosis.

claim: Tem1 is activated when a SPB enters the bud.
source: Tem1 is activated when a SPB enters the bud (Bardin et al., 2000; Pereira et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Cdc15 phosphorylates Nud1 to create a docking site for Dbf2-Mob1.
source: Cdc15 first phosphorylates the MEN scaffold Nud1, a core component of the SPB outer plaque. This phosphorylation creates a docking site for Dbf2-Mob1 on Nud1, facilitating phosphorylation and activation of Dbf2-Mob1 by Cdc15 (Mah et al., 2001; Rock et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Activation of Cdc15 depends on Cdc5 activity.
source: activation of Cdc15 depends on Cdc5 activity (Rock and Amon, 2011) which occurs only in mitosis (Cheng et al., 1998)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: CDKs phosphorylate Cdc15 and Mob1 thereby inhibiting their activity.
source: cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) phosphorylate Cdc15 and Mob1 thereby inhibiting their activity (Jaspersen and Morgan, 2000; König et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Cdc14 is sequestered in the nucleolus by its inhibitor Cfi1/Net1 from G1 until the onset of anaphase.
source: Cdc14 is sequestered in the nucleolus by its inhibitor Cfi1/Net1 from G1 until the onset of anaphase (Shou et al., 1999; Visintin et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The FEAR network promotes dissociation of Cdc14 from Cfi1/Net1 by facilitating phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1 by mitotic CDKs.
source: The FEAR network promotes dissociation of Cdc14 from Cfi1/Net1 by facilitating phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1 by mitotic CDKs (Azzam et al., 2004; Queralt et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Dbf2-Mob1 phosphorylates the NLS sequence in the C-terminus of Cdc14.
source: One contributing mechanism involves the phosphorylation of the nuclear localization signal (NLS) sequence in the C-terminus of Cdc14 by the MEN kinase Dbf2-Mob1 (Mohl et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Retention of Cdc14 in the cytoplasm is not required for mitotic exit.
source: However, retention of Cdc14 in the cytoplasm is not required for mitotic exit (Bembenek et al., 2005; Kuilman et al., 2015; Mohl et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Cfi1/Net1 is a potential Dbf2 substrate in vitro.
source: Proteome array screens for Dbf2-Mob1, the terminal kinase in the MEN, have identified Cfi1/Net1 as a potential Dbf2 substrate in vitro (Mah et al., 2001; Ptacek et al., 2005)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Cdc5 phosphorylates Cfi1/Net1.
source: In addition, the Polo-like kinase Cdc5, an important regulator of mitotic exit and essential for Cdc14 activation, has also been shown to phosphorylate Cfi1/Net1 (Loughrey Chen et al., 2002; Shou et al., 2002; Yoshida and Toh-e, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Mob1-eGFP at SPBs exhibits a rapid recovery with a half-recovery time of 4.6 ± 0.7 s after photobleaching.
source: We observed a rapid recovery of fluorescence with a half-recovery time of 4.6 ± 0.7 s (mean ± SD, n = 6 cells) after photobleaching of Mob1-eGFP fluorescence either at the daughter (dSPB) or the mother (mSPB) SPB.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Localization of Dbf2-Mob1 to SPBs is highly dynamic.
source: This fast turnover rate (~1/500 of the total duration for Dbf2-Mob1's SPB localization in anaphase) indicates that localization of Dbf2-Mob1 to SPBs is highly dynamic.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRAP data presented in the results.

claim: Mob1-eGFP transiently localizes to the nucleolus in late anaphase cells after nucleolar segregation.
source: Although subtle, we observed transient localization of Mob1-eGFP to the nucleolus in some cells as judged by co-localization with the nucleolar protein Cfi1/Net1. Importantly, this nucleolar localization was only observed in late anaphase cells after nucleolar segregation, when the MEN is normally active (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 1C.

claim: N-terminally truncated Mob1 mutants (Mob1Δ78 and Mob1Δ132) display increased nucleolar localization.
source: We found that they also displayed increased nucleolar localization (Figure 1D and F).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 1D and F.

claim: N-terminal truncation mutants of Mob1 partially suppress temperature sensitive alleles of cdc15-2 and tem1-3.
source: Indeed, we found that N-terminal truncation mutants of Mob1 partially suppressed temperature sensitive alleles of upstream MEN components (cdc15-2 and tem1-3; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a genetic suppression result shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Overexpression of Mob1 from the GPD promoter did not suppress the growth defect of cdc15-2 or tem1-3 mutants.
source: This suppression was not a result of elevated Mob1 protein levels because overexpression of Mob1 from the GPD promoter did not suppress the growth defect of cdc15-2 or tem1-3 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: This is a genetic suppression result shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Overexpression of Mob1 from the GPD promoter did not increase Mob1's nucleolar localization.
source: nor did it increase Mob1's nucleolar localization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Full-length Mob1 localizes to SPBs and the nucleolus during anaphase.
source: Full-length Mob1 localized to SPBs and the nucleolus during anaphase.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the localization pattern of Mob1.

claim: Mob1Δ78 and Mob1Δ132 display significantly greater nucleolar enrichment relative to full-length Mob1 in anaphase.
source: Consistent with earlier observations, the Mob1 truncations displayed significantly greater nucleolar enrichment relative to full-length Mob1 in anaphase (~30% and 120% increase on average for Mob1Δ78 and Mob1Δ132 respectively, Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Mob1Δ132 displays both greater and earlier nucleolar enrichment, evident already in metaphase.
source: In contrast, Mob1Δ132 displayed both greater and earlier nucleolar enrichment, evident already in metaphase.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the localization pattern of Mob1Δ132.

claim: Cfi1/Net1 was identified as the top hit for Mob1- and Dbf2-TurboID labeling.
source: In this experiment, we identified the nucleolar protein Cfi1/Net1 as the top hit for Mob1- and Dbf2-TurboID labeling (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a result from TurboID proximity-based labeling shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Cfi1/Net1 was only detected in the labeling experiments where Mob1 or Dbf2 was tagged with TurboID but not when Tem1 or Cdc15 was used as baits.
source: Importantly, Cfi1/Net1 was only detected in the labeling experiments where Mob1 or Dbf2 was tagged with TurboID but not when Tem1 or Cdc15 was used as baits (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a result from TurboID proximity-based labeling shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Nud1 was detected in the TurboID labeling experiments for all MEN proteins.
source: In contrast, Nud1, the MEN scaffold protein at SPBs, was detected in the TurboID labeling experiments for all MEN proteins (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a result from TurboID proximity-based labeling shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Slower migrating forms of Cfi1/Net1 were only observed in lysates obtained from cells expressing Mob1-TurboID.
source: Slower migrating forms of Cfi1/Net1 were only observed in lysates obtained from cells expressing Mob1-TurboID (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a result from streptavidin gel-shift assays shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mob1Δ78 and Mob1Δ132 no longer accumulate in the nucleolus during anaphase in cfi1/net1Δ cells.
source: While still localized to SPBs, Mob1Δ78 and Mob1Δ132 no longer accumulated in the nucleolus during anaphase in cfi1/net1Δ cells (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Overexpression of CFI1/NET1 from the GAL1-10 promoter increases nucleolar localization of both full-length and N-terminal truncation mutants of Mob1 by at least 50% (full-length) and up to 300% (truncations).
source: Furthermore, when we overexpressed CFI1/NET1 from the strong galactose-inducible GAL1-10 promoter, nucleolar localization of both full-length and N-terminal truncation mutants of Mob1 was increased by at least 50% (full-length) and up to 300% (truncations) (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Dbf2-Mob1 localization in the nucleolus during anaphase is mediated by interactions with Cfi1/Net1.
source: We conclude that Dbf2-Mob1 localization in the nucleolus during anaphase is mediated by interactions with Cfi1/Net1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TurboID and genetic experiments.

claim: Inhibition of cdc15-as1 prevented localization of Mob1 to SPBs and translocation of the MEN activity reporter NLSCdc14 into the cytoplasm.
source: As expected, inhibition of cdc15-as1 (through addition of the analog 1-NA-PP1) prevented localization of Mob1 to SPBs and translocation of the MEN activity reporter NLSCdc14 into the cytoplasm (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with cdc15-as1 inhibition shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Nucleolar localization of full-length Mob1 was significantly reduced when cdc15-as1 was inhibited.
source: Nucleolar localization of full-length Mob1 was also significantly reduced (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with cdc15-as1 inhibition shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Nucleolar localization of Mob1Δ78 and Mob1Δ132 was only moderately reduced when cdc15-as1 was inhibited.
source: Nucleolar localization of the N-terminally truncated Mob1Δ78 and Mob1Δ132 mutants, on the other hand, was only moderately reduced (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with cdc15-as1 inhibition shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mob1 localization to the nucleolus depends on MEN activity.
source: We conclude that Mob1 localization to the nucleolus depends on MEN activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cdc15-as1 inhibition experiments.

claim: In pre-anaphase cells, Dbf2-Mob1 was not captured by PhyB-Sik1 after 2 min of red-light activation.
source: Interestingly, in pre-anaphase cells, we were not able to capture a notable amount of nuclear Dbf2-Mob1 after 2 min of red-light activation.
evidence: This is a result from the PhyB-PIF optogenetics experiments.

claim: In anaphase cells in which the MEN is active, Dbf2-Mob1 was readily recruited to the nucleolus within 2 min by PhyB-Sik1.
source: In contrast, in anaphase cells in which the MEN is active, Dbf2-Mob1 was readily recruited to the nucleolus within 2 min (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from the PhyB-PIF optogenetics experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Nuclear access of Dbf2-Mob1 is cell cycle regulated.
source: we conclude that nuclear access of Dbf2-Mob1 is cell cycle regulated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the PhyB-PIF optogenetics experiments.

claim: In cells with wild-type CDC15, light-induced nucleolar recruitment of Mob1 was higher in anaphase than pre-anaphase cells.
source: In cells with wild-type CDC15, light-induced nucleolar recruitment of Mob1 was higher in anaphase than pre-anaphase cells.
evidence: This is a result from the PhyB-PIF optogenetics experiments.

claim: In cdc15-2 cells, the difference in light-induced nucleolar recruitment of Mob1 between anaphase and pre-anaphase was abolished.
source: In contrast, in cdc15-2 cells this difference was abolished (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a result from the PhyB-PIF optogenetics experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In addition to activating Dbf2's kinase activity, Cdc15 regulates Dbf2-Mob1's nuclear access.
source: We conclude that in addition to activating Dbf2's kinase activity (Mah et al., 2001), Cdc15 regulates Dbf2-Mob1's nuclear access.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the PhyB-PIF optogenetics experiments.

claim: Dbf2-Mob1 is a substrate of the nuclear exportin Crm1 in vitro.
source: Dbf2-Mob1 is a substrate of the nuclear exportin Crm1 in vitro (Kırlı et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Treatment of crm1T539C cells with LMB led to an increase in nucleolar localization of both full-length and N-terminally truncated Mob1.
source: Treatment of crm1T539C cells with LMB led to an increase in nucleolar localization of both full-length and N-terminally truncated Mob1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with LMB treatment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Crm1 controls nuclear export of Dbf2-Mob1.
source: suggesting that Crm1 controls nuclear export of Dbf2-Mob1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LMB treatment experiments.

claim: Overexpressed Mob1 was enriched in the nucleus.
source: Overexpressed Mob1 was enriched in the nucleus (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: When Mob1 was overexpressed together with Dbf2, Mob1 was no longer nuclear enriched.
source: In contrast, when we overexpressed Mob1 together with Dbf2, Mob1 was no longer nuclear enriched
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy.

claim: Dbf2 not Mob1 harbors a NES.
source: suggesting that Dbf2 not Mob1 harbors a NES.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the overexpression experiments.

claim: Inhibition of crm1T539C with LMB led to accumulation of Dbf2 in the nucleus.
source: Consistently, when overexpressed on its own, Dbf2 exhibited diffuse localization but inhibition of crm1T539C with LMB led to accumulation of Dbf2 in the nucleus (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Sequence analysis identified a putative NES sequence in the N-terminus of Dbf2 beginning with L12.
source: Sequence analysis identified a putative NES sequence in the N-terminus of Dbf2 beginning with L12 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Dbf2-HyA, when overexpressed, was nuclear enriched.
source: Dbf2-HyA, when overexpressed, was nuclear enriched (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Overexpressed DBF2 mutants where L12 had been mutated to either methionine (dbf2-L12M) or alanine (dbf2-L12A) accumulated in the nucleus.
source: Inspired by this observation, we overexpressed DBF2 mutants where L12 had been mutated to either methionine (dbf2-L12M) or alanine (dbf2-L12A). Both mutants accumulated in the nucleus (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The first 23 amino acids of Dbf2 were sufficient to drive nuclear export of eGFP.
source: Furthermore, we found that the first 23 amino acids of Dbf2 were sufficient to drive nuclear export of eGFP (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,G).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,G.

claim: dbf2-L12A mutation increases nucleolar localization of both full-length and N-terminally truncated Mob1 by at least 40%.
source: To test whether the NES in Dbf2 influences Dbf2-Mob1's nucleolar localization in anaphase under normal expression level, we characterized Mob1's cellular localization in dbf2-L12A and observed an increase in nucleolar localization by at least 40% for both full-length and N-terminally truncated Mob1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 3E.

claim: S17 and S20 within the NES of Dbf2 are phosphorylated in anaphase-arrested cells.
source: A previous phosphoproteomic study reported that S17 and S20 within the NES of Dbf2 are phosphorylated in anaphase-arrested cells (Holt et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Mutating S17 and S20 to phospho-mimetic residues (S17,20D or S17,20E) disrupted the NES.
source: We found that mutating S17 and S20 to phospho-mimetic residues (S17,20D or S17,20E) disrupted the NES
evidence: This is a result from the NES activity assays.

claim: Mutating S17 and S20 to alanine (S17,20A) retained the NES activity of Dbf2.
source: whereas mutating these residues to alanine (S17,20A) retained the NES activity of Dbf2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F and G).
evidence: This is a result from the NES activity assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F and G.

claim: The NES sequence in Dbf2 is well conserved among Saccharomycetes.
source: The NES sequence in Dbf2 is well conserved among Saccharomycetes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D)
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Inhibition of Cdc5 resulted in loss of Mob1's SPB localization and Dbf2-Mob1's kinase activity.
source: Consistent with the known functions of Cdc5 in MEN activation, we observed loss of Mob1's SPB localization and Dbf2-Mob1's kinase activity as monitored by translocation of the NLSCdc14 reporter into the cytoplasm when Cdc5 was inhibited (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with cdc5-as1 inhibition shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Nucleolar localization of Mob1, Mob1Δ78, and Mob1Δ132 was lost in cells lacking Cdc5 activity.
source: Nucleolar localization of Mob1, Mob1Δ78, and Mob1Δ132 was also lost in cells lacking Cdc5 activity (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with cdc5-as1 inhibition shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cdc5 regulates Dbf2-Mob1's nucleolar localization independently of its role in activating Cdc15.
source: These results suggested that Cdc5 regulates Dbf2-Mob1's nucleolar localization independently of its role in activating Cdc15.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cdc5-as1 inhibition experiments.

claim: When GAL-CDC15(1-750) was expressed, Mob1's SPB localization and Dbf2-Mob1's kinase activity was no longer restricted to anaphase but rather was high throughout the cell cycle.
source: When GAL-CDC15(1-750) was expressed, Mob1's SPB localization and Dbf2-Mob1's kinase activity was no longer restricted to anaphase but rather was high throughout the cell cycle as a result of MEN hyper-activation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with GAL-CDC15(1-750) expression shown in Figure 4B.

claim: GAL-CDC15(1-750) did not abolish cell-cycle regulation of Mob1's nucleolar localization but rather advanced it to early anaphase and metaphase.
source: Interestingly, GAL-CDC15(1-750) did not abolish cell-cycle regulation of Mob1's nucleolar localization but rather advanced it to early anaphase and metaphase (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with GAL-CDC15(1-750) expression shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In cells expressing GAL-CDC15(1-750), inactivation of CDC5 still abolished nucleolar localization of both full-length and the hyperactive N-terminally truncated Mob1 while Mob1 binding to SPBs was unaffected.
source: In cells expressing GAL-CDC15(1-750), inactivation of CDC5 still abolished nucleolar localization of both full-length and the hyperactive N-terminally truncated Mob1 while Mob1 binding to SPBs was unaffected (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy with GAL-CDC15(1-750) expression and cdc5-as1 inhibition shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Nucleolar localization of Dbf2-Mob1 directly depends on Cdc5 independently of its role in MEN activation.
source: These results demonstrate that nucleolar localization of Dbf2-Mob1 directly depends on Cdc5 independently of its role in MEN activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the GAL-CDC15(1-750) and cdc5-as1 inhibition experiments.

claim: Maximum enrichment of Mob1 in the nucleolus was not reduced in slk19Δ cells for all three forms of Mob1.
source: Importantly, maximum enrichment of Mob1 in the nucleolus was not reduced in slk19Δ cells for all three forms of Mob1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cdc5 regulates Dbf2-Mob1's nucleolar localization through mechanisms in addition to its role in the MEN and the FEAR network.
source: We conclude that Cdc5 regulates Dbf2-Mob1's nucleolar localization through mechanisms in addition to its role in the MEN and the FEAR network.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the slk19Δ experiments.

claim: Phosphoproteomic analyses identified 44 of the 64 previously known sites in Cfi1/Net1 and 18 new sites.
source: This analysis identified 44 of the 64 previously known sites in Cfi1/Net1 and 18 new sites (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses.

claim: IP-MS for Cfi1/Net1 in anaphase enriched cultures identified nine additional phosphorylation sites.
source: we also performed immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS) for Cfi1/Net1 in anaphase enriched cultures and identified nine additional sites (Supplementary file 4)
evidence: This is a result from IP-MS.

claim: A total of 91 phosphorylation sites were identified in Cfi1/Net1.
source: resulting in an astonishing total of 91 phosphorylation sites in Cfi1/Net1.
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses and IP-MS.

claim: 11 CDC15-dependent and 22 CDC5-dependent phosphorylation sites were identified in Cfi1/Net1.
source: Among them, we found 11 CDC15-dependent and 22 CDC5-dependent sites in Cfi1/Net1.
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses.

claim: Six of the CDC15-dependent sites fit Dbf2-Mob1's preferred sequence motif RXXS*.
source: Six of the CDC15-dependent sites fit Dbf2-Mob1's preferred sequence motif RXXS* (* represents the phosphorylation site) (Mah et al., 2005)
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses.

claim: 10 of the 11 CDC15-dependent phosphorylation sites in Cfi1/Net1 also depended on CDC5.
source: This was indeed the case for 10 of the 11 CDC15-dependent phosphorylation sites in Cfi1/Net1.
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses.

claim: 12 CDC5-only phosphorylation sites were identified in Cfi1/Net1.
source: To identify sites that only depended on CDC5 but not CDC15, we subtracted CDC15-dependent sites from CDC5-dependent sites yielding 12 sites (denoted as CDC5-only, Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses shown in Figure 5A.

claim: CDC15-dependent phosphorylation sites were concentrated in zone 2 of Cfi1/Net1.
source: CDC15-dependent phosphorylation sites were concentrated in zone 2, whereas CDC5-dependent sites were also found in zones 1 and 3.
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses.

claim: All the CDC5-dependent phosphorylation sites in Dbf2 and Mob1 were also CDC15-dependent.
source: In contrast to Cfi1/Net1, all the CDC5-dependent phosphorylation sites in Dbf2 and Mob1 were also CDC15-dependent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Cdc5 and Dbf2-Mob1 directly phosphorylate Cfi1/Net1.
source: These data indicate that Cdc5 and Dbf2-Mob1 directly phosphorylate Cfi1/Net1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phosphoproteomic analyses.

claim: Dbf2-Mob1 is a direct substrate of Cdc15 but not Cdc5.
source: Dbf2-Mob1 on the other hand is a direct substrate of Cdc15 but not Cdc5.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phosphoproteomic analyses.

claim: Cells harboring cfi1-91A as the sole source of CFI1/NET1 were viable and progressed through anaphase with only a slight delay in mitotic exit.
source: Cells harboring this allele as the sole source of CFI1/NET1 were viable and progressed through anaphase with only a slight delay in mitotic exit as judged by the timing of Mob1's dissociation from the SPBs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mob1Δ132 still localized to the SPBs during anaphase in cfi1-91A cells, but failed to accumulate in the nucleolus.
source: Interestingly, Mob1Δ132, which showed the most pronounced nucleolar localization among all Mob1 alleles analyzed, still localized to the SPBs during anaphase in cfi1-91A cells, but failed to accumulate in the nucleolus (Figure 5B and C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: Cfi1/Net1 phosphorylation is required for interacting with Dbf2-Mob1.
source: We conclude that Cfi1/Net1 phosphorylation is required for interacting with Dbf2-Mob1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cfi1-91A experiments.

claim: cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) abolished the nucleolar localization of Mob1Δ132.
source: Analysis of Mob1Δ132 localization in these mutants revealed that, similar to inhibition of Cdc5, cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) abolished the nucleolar localization of Mob1Δ132
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy.

claim: cfi1-Cdc15(z2) slightly increased nucleolar localization of Mob1Δ132.
source: while cfi1-Cdc15(z2) slightly increased nucleolar localization of the protein (Figure 5D and E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: The slower migrating form corresponding to biotinylated Cfi1/Net1 was absent in cells expressing cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) but present in cells expressing CFI or cfi1-Cdc15(z2).
source: The slower migrating form corresponding to biotinylated Cfi1/Net1 was absent in cells expressing cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) but present in cells expressing CFI or cfi1-Cdc15(z2) (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a result from streptavidin gel-shift assays shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1 by Cdc5 is required for Dbf2-Mob1 binding to the protein.
source: We conclude that phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1 by Cdc5 is required for Dbf2-Mob1 binding to the protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) experiments.

claim: 10 out of 12 CDC5-only sites identified in anaphase cells are already phosphorylated in cells arrested in metaphase using nocodazole.
source: First, consistent with the finding that Cdc5 is already active in metaphase, 10 out of 12 CDC5-only sites identified in anaphase cells are already phosphorylated in cells arrested in metaphase using the microtubule depolymerizing drug nocodazole (Figure 5—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is a result from phosphoproteomic analyses shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: There is considerable overlap between CDC5-dependent phosphorylation sites in vivo and sites identified in vitro.
source: Second, we found considerable overlap between CDC5-dependent phosphorylation sites in vivo and sites identified in vitro (Loughrey Chen et al., 2002; Shou et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a result from comparing in vivo and in vitro phosphorylation sites.

claim: Cdc5 and Cfi1/Net1 interact with each other in vivo as determined by TurboID labeling.
source: Third, Cdc5 and Cfi1/Net1 interact with each other in vivo as determined by TurboID labeling (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a result from TurboID labeling shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Cdc5 phosphorylates Cfi1/Net1 at the onset of metaphase which serves as a priming event for Dbf2-Mob1 binding to Cfi1/Net1 in anaphase.
source: We conclude that Cdc5 phosphorylates Cfi1/Net1 at the onset of metaphase which serves as a priming event for Dbf2-Mob1 binding to Cfi1/Net1 in anaphase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phosphoproteomic and TurboID experiments.

claim: The 3RA mutation in Mob1 abolished both the SPB and nucleolar localization of Mob1Δ132.
source: The 3RA mutation, while retaining nuclear access, abolished both the SPB and nucleolar localization of Mob1Δ132 (Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Dbf2-Mob1 binds to Cdc5-phosphorylated Cfi1/Net1 via Mob1's phosphoserine-threonine binding domain.
source: These data strongly support a model in which Dbf2-Mob1 binds to Cdc5-phosphorylated Cfi1/Net1 via Mob1's phosphoserine-threonine binding domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 3RA mutation experiments.

claim: Only phosphorylation in zone 2 of Cfi1/Net1 controlled Cdc14 release from Cfi1/Net1.
source: This analysis revealed that only phosphorylation in zone 2 controlled Cdc14 release from Cfi1/Net1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Mutating the phosphorylation sites in zone 2 also affected the ability of Cfi1/Net1 to bind Cdc14.
source: It is important to note that mutating the phosphorylation sites in zone 2 also affected the ability of Cfi1/Net1 to bind Cdc14, as judged by the lower degree of Cdc14 nucleolar sequestration prior to anaphase and localization of Cdc14 to the dSPB prior to anaphase (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Cells harboring cfi1/net1-6Cdk caused Cdc14 release defects similar to those of FEAR network mutants.
source: As reported previously (Azzam et al., 2004), cells harboring a CFI1/NET1 allele with six CDK sites mutated to alanine, cfi1/net1-6Cdk, caused Cdc14 release defects similar to those of FEAR network mutants (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Mutating the CDC15-dependent phosphorylation sites in zone 2 (cfi1-Cdc15(z2)) resulted in a significant reduction of Cdc14 release from the nucleolus but only recapitulated ~50% of the effect of inactivating CDC15.
source: Mutating the CDC15-dependent phosphorylation sites in zone 2 (cfi1-Cdc15(z2)) resulted in a significant reduction of Cdc14 release from the nucleolus but only recapitulated ~50% of the effect of inactivating CDC15 (compare Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Mutating the CDC5-only phosphorylation sites in zone 2 (cfi1-Cdc5only(z2)) resulted in a similar reduction of Cdc14 release from the nucleolus as inhibiting Cdc5.
source: Mutating the CDC5-only phosphorylation sites in zone 2 (cfi1-Cdc5only(z2)) resulted in a similar reduction of Cdc14 release from the nucleolus (Figure 6B) as inhibiting Cdc5.
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Combining cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) with cfi1-Cdc15(z2) (cfi1-Cdc15&Cdc5(z2)) caused an even greater defect in Cdc14 release from the nucleolus than either mutant alone.
source: Finally, combining cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) with cfi1-Cdc15(z2) (cfi1-Cdc15&Cdc5(z2)) caused an even greater defect in Cdc14 release from the nucleolus than either mutant alone (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Both cfi1-Cdc15(z2) and cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) mutant cells exited mitosis with an average delay of ~6 min (~25% increase).
source: Both cfi1-Cdc15(z2) and cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) mutant cells exited mitosis with an average delay of ~6 min (~25% increase, Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6C.

claim: cfi1-Cdc15&Cdc5(z2) double mutant cells exhibited a similar delay in mitotic exit as the cfi1-Cdc15(z2) and cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) single mutants.
source: Surprisingly, cfi1-Cdc15&Cdc5(z2) double mutant cells which had the most severe defect in Cdc14 release from the nucleolus exhibited a similar delay in mitotic exit as the cfi1-Cdc15(z2) and cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) single mutants
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy.

claim: Elevated levels of Cdc14 at dSPB were observed in both cfi1-Cdc15(z2) and cfi1-Cdc15&Cdc5(z2) cells prior to anaphase.
source: We observed elevated levels of Cdc14 at dSPB, indicating the presence of free Cdc14 not sequestered in the nucleolus, in both cfi1-Cdc15(z2) and cfi1-Cdc15&Cdc5(z2) cells prior to anaphase (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Cells expressing cdc14-3A instead of CDC14 exited from mitosis without significant delays.
source: Interestingly, cells expressing cdc14-3A instead of CDC14 exited from mitosis without significant delays (Figure 6—figure supplement 4B)
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Cytoplasmic retention of Cdc14 does not play a major role in promoting mitotic exit.
source: indicating that cytoplasmic retention of Cdc14 does not play a major role in promoting mitotic exit.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cdc14-3A experiments.

claim: The cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) mutant was synthetic lethal with the FEAR network mutants slk19Δ and spo12Δ.
source: Consistent with this idea, we found that the cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) mutant, which does not display defects in sequestering Cdc14 prior to anaphase, was synthetic lethal with the FEAR network mutants slk19Δ and spo12Δ (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a result from plasmid shuffling shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Combining cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) with the FEAR mutant cfi1-6Cdk resulted in severe defects in both FEAR network and MEN mediated Cdc14 release.
source: Furthermore, combining cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) with the FEAR mutant cfi1-6Cdk resulted in severe defects in both FEAR network and MEN mediated Cdc14 release (Figure 6—figure supplement 5A)
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5A.

claim: Combining cfi1-Cdc5only(z2) with cfi1-6Cdk resulted in ~20 min delays in both mitotic exit and nucleolar segregation.
source: and ~20 min delays in both mitotic exit and nucleolar segregation (Figure 6—figure supplement 5B), the strongest defect in all mutants we have characterized.
evidence: This is a result from live-cell microscopy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5B.

claim: CDC5 and MEN-dependent phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1 controls the protein's binding to Cdc14 and exit from mitosis.
source: We conclude that CDC5 and MEN-dependent phosphorylation of Cfi1/Net1 controls the protein's binding to Cdc14 and exit from mitosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Cfi1/Net1 phospho-mutant experiments.
